vintage: Built 2026-10-27. Homes: ACS 2024 5-year. Outages, customers, choice, markets, batteries, and programs: EIA-861 calendar 2025, final release 7 Oct 2026. Storm and heat: FEMA National Risk Index counties, version December 2025, queried 2026-10-27.

factors.label: Owner-occupied single-family homes
factors.help: Census ACS 2024 5-year, table B25032. Owner-occupied one-unit detached plus one-unit attached. Large states score higher here.

factors.label: Outage duration (SAIDI)
factors.help: EIA-861 2025 state total, including major events. Minutes per customer. Longer outages raise the score, as a backup-battery signal.

factors.label: Outage frequency (SAIFI)
factors.help: EIA-861 2025 state total, including major events. Interruptions per customer. More frequent outages raise the score.

factors.label: Storm risk
factors.help: FEMA National Risk Index. County hurricane, tornado, hail, ice storm, strong wind, winter weather, and lightning scores, averaged and weighted by county population.

factors.label: Heat-wave risk
factors.help: FEMA National Risk Index heat-wave score, weighted by county population.

factors.label: Retail delivery share
factors.help: Share of residential customers served by a delivery utility. Texas wires companies come from EIA's delivery-companies file. Retail-only suppliers are removed first so the same Texas home is not counted twice.

factors.label: Wholesale market share
factors.help: Share of residential customers whose balancing authority is an ISO or RTO in EIA's 2025 authority list: CAISO, ERCOT, ISO-NE, MISO, NYISO, PJM, or SPP, detected from the authority's name.

factors.label: Residential batteries per 1,000 customers
factors.help: EIA-861 2025 net-metered residential batteries, paired with solar plus standalone, per 1,000 residential customers.

factors.label: Demand response per 1,000 customers
factors.help: Residential demand-response enrollments reported on EIA-861 2025, per 1,000 residential customers. Blank cells are left out of the sum.

factors.label: Dynamic pricing per 1,000 customers
factors.help: Residential dynamic-pricing enrollments reported on EIA-861 2025, per 1,000 residential customers. Blank cells are left out of the sum.

ercot.summary: Day-ahead settlement point prices, ERCOT report NP4-190-CD (12331), 32 delivery dates (2026-09-27 through 2026-10-28). Basis is the resource-node price minus its settlement load zone in the same hour. 1043 resource nodes had at least 100 comparable hours. The settlement-point file is CIM_Oct_ML3_1_10272026_SP_List_and_EB_Mapping. The public price file has no coordinates, so the nodes are a table.
notes: A positive basis means the node cleared higher than its load zone in the day-ahead market. Losses and congestion are both inside that spread. There is no shift-factor file here, so a constraint is not assigned to a node.
The $20 threshold counts hours. It is a label for this note, not an ERCOT rule. This window is the files posted on the public list at build time, not a calendar year.

Shadow prices are ERCOT report NP4-191-CD, DAM Shadow Prices. Hours count rows with a positive shadow price on the same delivery dates. One constraint can bind under more than one contingency, so the hour count can run past the length of the window.

omitted.title: Permitting speed
omitted.reason: The SolarAPP+ locations CSV on gosolarapp.org returned HTTP 403. The public HTML table contained 100 jurisdictions and stopped alphabetically at Del Norte, so it is not a state census. It is not in the score.

omitted.title: Home-battery interconnection time
omitted.reason: No machine-readable national series of residential permission-to-operate times was retrieved. Berkeley Lab's Queued Up measures generator interconnection, a different queue, so it is not used as a home-battery proxy.

omitted.title: Price volatility outside ERCOT
omitted.reason: A comparable public nodal series was not pulled for PJM, MISO, CAISO, or the other markets. Those states are not given a zero on a grid-value factor. Texas is a separate section.

omitted.title: DSIRE incentives
omitted.reason: State battery rebates were not scraped into this build. Program activity is EIA-861 enrollment and net-metered battery counts, which is a different fact from a rebate existing on paper.

narrative: At equal weights, Michigan (76), Texas (71), and Maryland (69) lead the 51 geographies. Michigan's strongest public signals on this scale are outage duration (saidi) (98) and demand response per 1,000 customers (92). Read the score as a stack of percentiles. A high score means the public series line up. It is an outside view, with no Base install times, permit outcomes, or crew plan in it.

The home-count factor rewards size. California has the most owner-occupied single-family homes, 6,771,188. With that weight set to zero, the top three become Michigan (75), Maryland (70), and Texas (68).

Base's public footprint, marked on the map and kept out of the weights: Texas ranks 2 (score 71), with SAIDI 225 minutes, retail delivery share 56.2%, and wholesale mix ERCOT 88%, MISO 5%, SPP 5%. Illinois ranks 8 (score 60), with SAIDI 144 minutes, retail delivery share 22.1%, and wholesale mix PJM 71%, MISO 29%. Georgia ranks 30 (score 47), with SAIDI 270 minutes, retail delivery share 0.0%, and wholesale mix No ISO balancing authority. Connecticut ranks 19 (score 54), with SAIDI 211 minutes, retail delivery share 15.8%, and wholesale mix ISO-NE 100%.

Georgia's largest balancing authority in this file is Southern Company Services, Inc. - Trans. EIA reports no residential delivery service there. A utility contract, the shape of the reported Central Georgia EMC project, does not appear in the retail-choice factor, so Georgia's rank is a weak guide to that path.

The longest state SAIDI in this file is West Virginia at 1013 minutes. The highest residential delivery share is Massachusetts at 61.5%. Commonwealth Edison reports 3,753,924 residential customers, SAIDI 77 minutes, and wholesale tag PJM. Central Georgia (Central Georgia El Member Corp) reports 62,546 residential customers and SAIDI 168 minutes.
Install friction and a national price-volatility series sit outside the score. The Texas section is a short public day-ahead window, a congestion example rather than a yearly value of the nodes.

From 2026-09-27 through 2026-10-28, KNAPP_RN in LZ_WEST (substation KNAPP) had a 95th-percentile day-ahead basis of $196.68/MWh across 768 hours, and 53% of those hours cleared at least $20/MWh above the zone. The median resource node in LZ_HOUSTON had a 95th-percentile basis of $6.36/MWh. The constraint with the most positive shadow-price rows was 6437__F.
